messages:
mike: Heads-up — we saw a tenant causing long queues during the EU primetime and it pushed other tenants' p95s over the SLO. Thinking we should sketch a tenant-rate-shed strategy that is fair but lightweight. Thoughts?

tara: +1. Are you thinking strict per-tenant rate caps or admission sampling? strict caps can waste spare capacity, sampling keeps high-util tenants in the mix. :thinking:

yun: If we sample, we need to consider streaming requests. Preempting midstream will produce partial responses and retries. That interacts badly with our hedging/fallbacks.

mike: Right. Two constraints: 1) preserve low-latency tail for small/paid tenants, 2) avoid expensive stateful ops to decide admit/drop. Proposal: per-tenant token-budget window + probabilistic admit when over-budget. Cheap approx: maintain two counters per tenant (tokens_in_window, last_tick) updated atomically.

tara: Probabilistic admit helps. For fairness across tenants of different traffic shapes, maybe use a token-weighted reservoir sampling for admits: higher-prob tenants get more slots but share proportionally. Also keep a minimal guaranteed throughput for gold customers.

yun: Implementation caveats: 1) KV cache locality — if we drop midstream we lose warm KV cache for that session; 2) retries — clients will often retry immediately, causing bursts. We should couple shed decisions with a short retry-backoff hint header so clients can backoff.

mike: Agreed. Example admit policy sketch (very rough):
```json
{
  "window_ms": 1000,
  "per_tenant_tokens": 1000,
  "prob_admit_formula": "min(1, tokens_left / expected_tokens)",
  "guarantees": {"gold": 0.1}
}
```

tara: What about fairness when tenants send many small streaming calls vs big single calls? Token accounting should be token-weighted (tokens ~ bytes or tokens generated) rather than call-count. That avoids starving heavy-call tenants that are actually costlier.

yun: For streaming, maybe we classify requests as short vs long at admission time (cheap fast path). If a long stream is admitted, pin it to a quota bucket that is charged incrementally (so we don't preempt after many tokens have been emitted). If we decide to preempt, we should prefer preempting new admits, not midstream.

mike: Good point. So algorithm: admit decision at request start (token-estimate prediction), if predicted_long -> admit only if bucket has >threshold; else probabilistic admit. For streams we emit header `X-Redwood-Shed-Hint: retry-after=100` on drops.

tara: We should measure two metrics for experiments: p95 latency for small tenants, and aggregate token-throttled ratio for large tenants. Also track cache-warmth loss (KV hit-rate delta) when shed is active.

yun: Ops note: implement as an ingress filter in frontdoor (cheap in C++) to keep runtime overhead low. Add a metrics tag `shed_active=true` to traces when shedding decisions were applied.

mike: I'll make a short RFC with the admit pseudocode + experiment plan. Action items: mike -> RFC, tara -> sampling sim harness, yun -> add trace metric and header support. ops-bot: create experiment ticket? :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-8421 for tenant-shed experiment and linked to the thread.
